source: Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces; water, ice, wind and plant roots all do it. Erosion carries the pieces away, and they are dropped somewhere else, building new land.
Thinking weathering and erosion are the same. Weathering breaks the rock; erosion moves the pieces.
The Grand Canyon is more than a mile deep. A river did most of the digging, a grain at a time, over millions of years.
Weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces. Erosion carries the pieces away. Deposition drops them somewhere else, where they build new land.
Things that weather and erode the land.
Rivers drop their sand and mud where they slow down, often where they meet the sea. That builds a delta, like the Nile Delta or the Mississippi Delta.
Rain washes soil off a bare hillside into a stream. Weathering or erosion?
The soil was already in small pieces.
Thinking weathering and erosion are the same. Weathering breaks; erosion moves.
